facts.statement: Riojasaurus was named by José Bonaparte after the La Rioja Province in Argentina where its fossils were found.
facts.quote: Riojasaurus (meaning "lizard from La Rioja") was a herbivorous sauropodomorph dinosaur named after La Rioja Province in Argentina where it was found in the Los Colorados Formation in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin by José Bonaparte.

facts.statement: Riojasaurus lived during the Late Triassic Norian stage and grew to about 6.6 meters long.
facts.quote: It lived during the Late Triassic (Norian stage) and grew to about 6.6 m long.

facts.statement: The first cranial material of Riojasaurus incertus was discovered in 1987 and described in 1995.
facts.quote: In total, at least twenty specimens have been assigned to R. incertus, and the first cranial material of R. incertus was discovered in 1987 and described in 1995.

facts.statement: In 1994, 56 caudal vertebrae, a skull cast, and other specimens of Riojasaurus incertus were stolen from the National University of La Rioja.
facts.quote: In 1994, 56 caudal vertebrae from one specimen, and a cast of the skull of Riojasaurus incertus, along with several other specimens, were stolen from the National University of La Rioja in Argentina.

facts.statement: Riojasaurus had dense and massive leg bones, which were unusual for an early sauropodomorph.
facts.quote: Its leg bones were dense and massive for an early sauropodomorph.

facts.statement: Riojasaurus is thought to have moved slowly on all fours and been unable to stand on its hind legs.
facts.quote: It has been thought it probably moved slowly on all fours and was unable to rear up on its back legs.

facts.statement: Some researchers interpret the hand and shoulder girdle morphology as inconsistent with a quadrupedal gait.
facts.quote: However, the morphology of the hand and shoulder girdle has been interpreted as inconsistent with a quadrupedal gait.

facts.statement: Riojasaurus had leaf-shaped and serrated teeth.
facts.quote: The teeth of Riojasaurus were leaf shaped and serrated.

facts.statement: The upper jaw of Riojasaurus contained 5 front teeth and 24 additional teeth in a row ending under the eyes.
facts.quote: The upper jaw contained 5 teeth at the front, with 24 more behind them in a row that ended under the eyes.

facts.statement: Due to its size and limb anatomy, Riojasaurus has been considered a close relative of the earliest sauropods.
facts.quote: Due to their size and limb anatomy Riojasaurus and the possibly related Melanorosaurus have been considered close relatives of the earliest sauropods.

facts.statement: Riojasaurus lived between 218 and 211 million years ago during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace entre 218 y 211 millones de años, durante el Noriense, y en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Riojasaurus measured approximately 11 meters long and 3 meters high, with an estimated weight of 800 kg to 3 tonnes.
facts.quote: Riojasaurus medía aproximadamente 11 metros de largo y 3 de alto, presentando un peso estimado de unos 800 kilos a 3 toneladas.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated Riojasaurus to be 6.6 meters long and weigh 800 kilograms.
facts.quote: En 2010 Gregory S. Paul estimó su longitud en 6,6 metros y su peso en 800 kilogramos.

facts.statement: In 2016, Scott Hartman found that the hand anatomy, straight back, and immobile shoulder girdle supported a bipedal interpretation for Riojasaurus.
facts.quote: En 2016, Scott Hartman descubrió que la anatomía de la mano, la espalda relativamente recta y la cintura escapular en gran parte inmóvil de Riojasaurus lo respaldaban como bípedo.

facts.statement: Riojasaurus is closely related to Eucnemesaurus from South Africa, forming the family Riojasauridae within the Prosauropoda group.
facts.quote: Está estrechamente emparentado con Eucnemesaurus de Sudáfrica, formando entre ellos la familia de los Riojasauridae dentro del grupo Prosauropoda.

facts.statement: Riojasaurus is now considered more basal than Melanorosaurus.
facts.quote: Hoy es considerado más basal que Melanorosaurus

facts.statement: It is debated whether prosauropods and sauropods share a common ancestor, a hypothesis proposed by Peter Galton and Paul Sereno.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, si la hipótesis propuesta por Peter Galton y Paul Sereno es correcta, los prosaurópodos y los saurópodos compartirían un ancestro común.

facts.statement: Riojasaurus lived from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago during the Norian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
